newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica mulls foreign tranche cut-press.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica mulls foreign tranche cut-press.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica is considering cutting the number of shares it will offer to foreign institutions in order to meet strong domestic demand in its privatisation next month, local media said on Wednesday.

Spanish daily Expansion reported that Telefonica and state holding company SEPPa could increase the tranche offered to domestic investors to 75 percent from a previously allocated 58 percent, in the privatisation of the government's remaining 20.9 percent stake.
A Telefonica spokesman declined to comment on the reports on Wednesday morning and a SEPPa spokesman was not available to comment.
In an interview with British daily the Financial Times, Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga said his basic priority was to increase the number of shareholders.
"Every one who wants shares in Spain will have them," Villalonga said.
